notes: Maps every N02 invariant to the golden scenarios that exercise it (crates/franken-control/tests/vectors/n02_scenarios.json) and to the Rust tests under crates/franken-control/src/channel that check it.

tests/n02/test_reference_model.py verifies the mapping: each scenario names only declared invariants, each invariant has at least one scenario, each listed Rust test exists, and docs/contracts/n02.md mentions each invariant.
Everything here is host simulation of a message-handling state machine. It says nothing about a network, a real MAC, a board or an audible result.

invariants.claim: A request that does not authenticate changes nothing: no queue, no ledger entry, no rate-limit allowance.
When the acknowledgement of a committed command is lost, the retry is answered with the recorded outcome and the command is not applied again.
However many times a command is delivered, it takes effect at most once.
A duplicated relative volume change applies exactly one delta, whether the copy arrives before or after the original is applied.
A storm of retries leaves queue length and ledger size unchanged and produces one effect.
The same command number with different content is refused, while the first is waiting and after it settled.
After the retention period an outcome is forgotten, and a retry is answered as unknown (never re-applied).
When the ledger is full the oldest outcome is forgotten explicitly, and newer ones are still answered.
Exactly-once is not promised forever: beyond the window the channel reports unknown and does not guess.
A controller acting under an old epoch changes nothing once the group's epoch has moved on.
A key bound to one epoch is refused at the door under any other epoch.
Nothing the channel applies can advance the group's epoch, so a request cannot fence out the legitimate leader.
A command whose expected revision is not the current one is refused with no effect.
A peer revoked or rebound after its command was accepted has no effect when the command would run.
Every queue is bounded; a full lane refuses new work, and a refusal for want of room does not consume the command number.
A request turned away before acceptance can be sent again unchanged once the reason has passed.
A command refused after acceptance has its refusal recorded as its outcome, and a retry is told the same.
Rate limits are per authenticated peer and per lane, and refusals state the exact wait.
Stop, mute and cancel travel in a separate lane that is served before ordinary work.
A local stop is applied in the first step after it is accepted, ahead of every queued remote command, through a full queue and a remote flood.
The local user keeps priority slots a remote peer cannot take, and the lane is still bounded.
Priority never bypasses authentication: a forged stop is refused like any forged request.
The local user is not refused for epoch or expected revision; a remote controller in the same position is.
An accepted command that waits longer than the pending limit expires unapplied, and that is its recorded outcome.
No retry or wait is unbounded: queue time, ledger memory and rate are all limited.
Cancel withdraws a waiting ordinary command of the same peer before it commits, and changes nothing after, for another peer, or against a stop.
Relative volume is resolved against the live value in the channel and clamped to 0..=100.
A step applies at most its budget of commands; the rest wait for the next step.

A session refusal that is not about the command's content (a repeated or out-of-window number, a stale epoch) is an internal fault: counted, kept for the operator, recorded without detail and never shown to the sender. An unknown member is still the sender's.
After a channel restart against a session that kept running, a copy composed before the restart is refused whatever its kind, nothing is reverted, and a command composed after the restart is applied.
A restarted channel numbers its session commands above everything its predecessor used, so the first commands after a restart are not session faults.

Absolute volume stays naturally repeatable: a command composed against an older revision than the current one still applies within an incarnation, so pipelined updates and interleaved controllers are not stale.
A remote controller's volume or mute command must name the revision it last read, or it is turned away at the door without consuming its number; stop, cancel and the local user need none.
A command naming a revision the session has not reached is refused with no effect.

A command that changes the group is applied only under a live group lease (a G01 AuthorityToken the session still accepts at the time of the step); with none, a superseded one or an expired one it is refused before the session is touched.
After the issuer advances the epoch, a late command under the old lease is refused, and the same command is applied once the new epoch's lease is installed.
A lease is live up to the instant before its expiry and refused from that instant; renewal plus resubmit is applied.
A lease the session does not accept (foreign issuer or group, stale, future, already expired) cannot be installed, and the lease already held keeps working.
A refusal for want of a live lease is reported but not recorded, so the same request sent again after the lease is installed or renewed is judged afresh.
A local stop and a local mute-on only silence and need no lease; a cancel only withdraws its sender's waiting work and needs none.
A forged request fails authentication before the lease is consulted.
Every command that reaches a terminal outcome in a step is written to the log exactly once, with its correlation id, the committed revision, the epoch, the queue depth and the time it waited.

invariants.claim: When the harness names an injected fault (LogConfig::with_fault), every kind of record the log writes (a settled command, an acknowledgement, a request turned away at submit, the closing record) carries it as the shared schema's fault, between latency_us and cause, and the record parses as a DiagnosticEvent and round-trips byte for byte; a log told no fault writes the records it always wrote, with no fault key (each fault line is its base line plus the pair); the label is held to the label alphabet and 64 bytes and at its limit no record passes the line cap; a log never told the fault, one under another fault, one whose records of a single kind forget it, and a run under no fault whose records name one are each reported by name. The label only names what the run was under: the channel injects no fault.

invariants.claim: With a clock-uncertainty margin u the held lease stops being usable u before its expiry, exactly where G01's own liveness rule stops it; a lease with no more than u left cannot be installed.

A holder whose lease is about to expire renews it through a quorum win and keeps applying commands with no gap; a lapsed holder's renewal is refused and its commands stay refused until it wins a new epoch; a newer holder's adoption fences the old lease; a renewal needs a held lease and a quorum group and cannot be replayed to stretch the lease.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: Renewal needs G01's real quorum machinery (voters, rounds, wins), which the Python model does not model; the Rust tests drive G01's own LeaseVoter, QuorumRound and GroupMembership.

invariants.claim: A revocation survives a restart if the owner stores the tombstone snapshot and restores it into a fresh directory first: the stale admission of a revoked identity is refused at or below its tombstone, the key is answered Revoked exactly as before the restart, a deliberate re-admission one version up works, a malformed snapshot is refused whole, and a restart that forgets, mis-versions or restores a stale snapshot lets the revoked key back or leaves it refused for the wrong reason (the judge catches each by name).
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: The Python scenario model has no restart or persistence operation; the Rust tests judge it through the channel, with planted persistence faults.

invariants.claim: After a full process restart, a stored revision high-water mark restored before the first step raises the revision floor to at least the mark: a held-back copy composed against the old history is refused exactly as StaleRevision even after the rebuilt session climbs past its revision, a fresh command composed against the restored session is admitted, the local user is never affected, and a mark is accepted only before the first step; a restart that stores nothing or a stale mark admits the copy, one that overshoots locks fresh controllers out, and the judge catches each by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: The Python scenario model has no process restart or persisted mark; the Rust tests judge it through the channel with planted persistence faults.

invariants.claim: The channel's production source uses no thread, lock, atomic, Arc, clock read, file, socket, process, environment or unsafe, and under a six-thousand-operation flood every structure it keeps stays within its cap after every operation; the per-peer tables are bounded by the authority's identity cap, and an authority that admits every identity takes them past their caps and the census catches it.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the source text and of the structures' sizes under load, judged by Rust tests that read the channel's own files; the Python scenario model has nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: Through the real endpoint, channel and peer directory, over the six-thousand-operation flood, the host heap the channel holds stays within a bound written from its caps: one handle call peaks at most UNIT_COPIES request-sized units above where it started, one step at most max_per_step + 1 times that, and the live heap after every operation is under the sum of its stored records, per-peer rows and log ring; it does not grow with the requests already served, and the bound shrinks with the caps; a channel whose authority keeps every message it verifies breaks the retained bound by name, one that takes a large scratch buffer per message breaks the datagram peak by name, and each check is judged alone on synthetic runs. Host heap only: not the stack, a thread census, a device or a guest. The durable step is also measured with relative commands: sixteen admitted identities each send relative commands, each accepted by one durable step (a floor reservation, the 226-byte floors record, a copy of the session, the mark), over a journal loaded to the device limits so that it compacts a full snapshot repeatedly; the floors and the mark are restored from the medium through the restore calls and equal what the running channel held; the step is judged against the formula written from the caps with no allowance for the session copy or the compaction, and its components are printed.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: This is a property of the host heap under load, measured by a counting global allocator in franken-alloc-probe (the workspace forbids unsafe in franken-control); the Python scenario model has no allocator and nothing to say about it.

invariants.claim: The revision high-water mark is stored on U01's journal after each step and read back at boot: after a process death, only the durable bytes survive, a held-back copy is refused exactly as StaleRevision, a fresh command applies and the journal then holds the new mark; an owner that never restores, and one whose first process never stored, admit the copy and the judge catches each by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: step_then_store returns a step's outcomes only after the mark that covers them is durable, and withholds them if the store fails; with the power cut at every storage operation and byte budget of one store the recovered mark is exactly the old or the new one, and the duplicate of every delivered command is refused; an owner that delivers before it stores is caught by the sweep, and one that forgot to restore cannot store over the mark.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: A journal that cannot be read (opening fails, or neither segment is valid) gives the channel the floor u64::MAX instead of the session's revision: for that run every remote command that names a revision is refused as StaleRevision, the local user still commits, and the floor is never stored; an owner that treats the unreadable journal as no mark admits the copy and the judge catches it by name.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about either.

invariants.claim: A relative command's identity floor (the highest number the channel has begun to apply for it) is made durable in the record n02.seq before the command's effect, and a retry at or below a floor is answered OutOfWindow at submit and never applied. With the power cut at every storage operation and byte budget of a relative command's two stores (its floor, then the mark), for the local user (whose commands the revision checks never reach) and for a controller, the recovered floor is exactly the old one or the new one; the duplicate of every delivered command is unknown after the restart (OutOfWindow, never queued); a command that was not delivered is unknown if its floor was recorded and applies exactly once if it was not; a duplicate with a bad proof is Unauthenticated, not OutOfWindow. An owner that steps without reserving, one that delivers before it stores, one that leaves a withheld outcome in the ledger, and one that steps the live session instead of a copy each fail the sweep by name (ADMITTED, LAUNDERED, NOT-STAGED).
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: A durable step is a transaction. It runs on a copy of the session, and the copy replaces the session only after the mark is durable. If the store fails, the ledger gives back what the step recorded and every older outcome it evicted (with the floors it had raised), the counters are restored, the log facts it gathered are dropped, one critical record says a store failed, and the retry is later logged exactly once. An idle poll, and a step that cannot have moved the mark (every command refused), stage nothing and do not call the journal, so a journal poisoned from outside fails a pure refusal never and a step that needs the mark always. A rejection waiting in the log when a durable step begins is written once, before the step, against the live session's revision (never the copy's), whether the store then fails or succeeds.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: The first store that fails latches the channel's durable path failed. While latched nothing is staged and no journal call is made; the local user's stop and mute-on are applied to the live session, a cancel still withdraws, and every other command (relative or absolute, from any role, a controller's stop included) is refused as InternalFault with the cause durability_failed and is not recorded, so the same request can be sent again; nothing that raises volume gets through. Only reopen_from_open clears the latch: the channel then offers at least the mark the medium holds (a write the medium took despite the error does not lock it out as MarkRegressed) and keeps the larger of each identity's floor; a medium that cannot be opened leaves the latch. The first accepted local stop or mute-on that itself discovers the failure (also when another writer poisoned the journal) is applied to the live session and delivered (StoreFailed::applied) while a co-queued volume increase, relative step or unmute stays unapplied and withheld; a revoked or forged mute-on is not applied. The one critical record of a failed step names a command that stays withheld, never a silence that is then applied (a step of only silences still writes it, naming number 0). Across a process boundary, over a regular file with one chosen program or sync failure injected (harness, unix only): the panel's mute-on is answered 200, is applied to the live session and the plane is latched at that step; a controller's volume set and the panel's unmute are refused with the volume unchanged and the member still muted; the file keeps its old mark, and a fresh process without the fault restores it and applies the same three steps in full; after a failed sync the file holds the old or the new mark and nothing else. These are three SEQUENTIAL requests, checked by the process_restart group in other_rust_checks, and they are NOT evidence for the one-step property stated above (the mute-on applied while the set and the unmute of the same step are withheld), which only the in-process step_then_store tests evidence.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: Only relative commands of an identity with a stable retry number reserve a floor. An identity declared with declare_unstable_retry_ids (the legacy bridge, which composes a fresh number per request) gets none: forty of its relative commands write one frame each (the mark) and no n02.seq record, and its duplicate after a restart is not answered OutOfWindow (no dedup is claimed); a stable identity's relative command writes the floor and then the mark. Absolute and stop commands record nothing. A floor that cannot be stored refuses the relative command untouched (InternalFault, cause store_<code>, recorded: send it under a new number) while a local absolute set and a stop still commit; a malformed record refuses every relative command for the run and leaves the others working; floors offered after the first step are an error; plain step reserves nothing.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: The floors are one record in the Records namespace, 2 + 14n bytes (226 for sixteen identities), canonical, and the decoder refuses everything else by name; sixteen identities fit the device journal and come back in full after a restart, a seventeenth is refused rather than evicting one, the smallest configuration holds two and refuses a third without poisoning the journal, the key fits both configurations, and merging two tables keeps the larger floors and refuses when the union does not fit. The record is the fourth and last of the device journal's four record slots.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: The plain development stepper and the in-memory journal stepper are named in no production file but the file that defines them, the one that re-exports them and the Q01 harness, so a production owner must write the name of a non-durable stepper to get one. A source scan over every crate's production sources shows it, and shows that it reads the production part only and sees a name there.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the channel over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection (and of the transaction around it), judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.

invariants.claim: boot_durable opens the journal, restores the revision mark and the relative-command floors and returns the stepper in one call, before the channel's first step: a blank medium boots with nothing to restore; a journal holding a mark and floors gives both to the channel and a restored floor is in force at once; a medium that cannot be opened boots latched and refusing; a journal with no valid state boots durable but refusing for the run; a channel that has already stepped is refused; and what a booted stepper stores is what the next boot over the same medium restores. The speaker's Virtual House control plane has a durable constructor over it (its campaign fixture stays volatile and says so): a restart over the same medium answers a delivered tailnet step 801 and applies a bridge step once. A latched owner is reopened in one call (reopen_durable): a medium that opens clears the latch and the new stepper stores again; one that cannot be opened leaves the latch; a journal ahead of the session is offered at its mark with its floors in force. A latched boot returns a stepper through which the local user's stop and mute-on work and a controller's command is refused, and which latches a channel that is not latched rather than step it volatilely. Over a regular file (the harness's FileMedium, unix only, no device medium) the same plane runs as a PROCESS: a new process restores the mark and the floors from the file alone (it is told only the session's revision and volume, which G01 does not store) and answers the delivered tailnet step 801 where a fresh file applies the identical request; a process killed after its acknowledged steps does the same for a fresh process; a file that is not the medium's is refused by name before any plane exists and left unchanged. A process kill keeps every byte already handed to the OS, so none of this is evidence of sync_all or of a power cut.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the owner's boot over U01's journal on an in-memory medium, judged by Rust tests; the Python scenario model has no journal.

invariants.claim: Peers admitted, revoked and rebound through custody come back after a process death from the durable bytes of U01's journal alone: a controller still commits with its key, a revoked key is refused exactly as Revoked, a rebound key is turned away at its old epoch and accepted at the new, the roles came back, a re-admission at the tombstone's version is refused as Resurrection and one version up with a new key works while the old key is BadProof; an owner that stores nothing, one that revokes only in memory, one that rebinds only in memory and one that never restores each fail the judge by name. The credentials and the revision mark share one journal and both come back.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the peer directory over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests through the channel; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them. The independent evidence is the Python mirror of the judges over U01's independent Python journal (its expected cut counts are the ones the Rust asserts) and the hand-written record bytes.

invariants.claim: An admission and a rebinding are stored before the directory changes (a failed store leaves it unchanged; an owner that admits first is caught); with the power cut at every storage operation and byte budget of each of the three stores the recovered state is exactly the old or the new one, a call that returned Ok has left the new one and an earlier admission is untouched; a rebinding written as a revocation then an admission is caught by the sweep.
invariants.scenario_inapplicable: These are properties of the peer directory over U01's journal on an in-memory medium with fault injection, judged by Rust tests through the channel; the Python scenario model has no journal and nothing to say about them.
